related_questions.question: How much do you get for one person on SNAP?

text_blocks.snippet: For one person, the maximum monthly SNAP (food stamps) benefit is $292. However, the actual amount received can vary based on income, expenses, and other factors. Most people receive less than the maximum amount.

list.title: Maximum Benefit:
list.snippet: The maximum benefit for a single person is $292 per month.

list.title: Varies by State:
list.snippet: SNAP benefits are administered by individual states, so there may be slight variations in eligibility rules and benefit amounts.

list.title: Income and Expenses:
list.snippet: SNAP benefits are based on a household's net income (income after deductions) and allowable expenses, such as rent, utilities, and childcare costs.

list.title: Calculating Benefits:
list.snippet: States use a formula to determine SNAP benefits, typically subtracting a percentage of a household's net income (often 30%) from the maximum benefit amount.

list.title: Example:
list.snippet: If a single person has a net income of $200 per month and the state expects them to contribute 30% of their income to food, their contribution would be $60 (30% of $200). Their SNAP benefit would then be $232 ($292 maximum benefit - $60 expected contribution).
